q: The Doctrine of Lapse was introduced by which Governor-General?
exp: Dalhousie (1848-56) annexed states such as Satara, Jhansi and Nagpur by the Doctrine of Lapse.

q: Indira Point, the southernmost point of India, is located in
exp: Indira Point (6°45'N) is in Great Nicobar Island of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

q: Which city of Bihar is popularly known as the 'Silk City'?
exp: Bhagalpur is famous for Tussar (Bhagalpuri) silk.

q: Fundamental Rights are contained in which Part of the Indian Constitution?
exp: Part III (Articles 12-35) contains Fundamental Rights.

q: India's first lunar probe, Chandrayaan-1, was launched in
exp: Chandrayaan-1 was launched by PSLV-C11 on 22 October 2008.

q: Which Gupta ruler is called the 'Napoleon of India' by V. A. Smith?
exp: Samudragupta's many conquests, recorded in the Allahabad Pillar inscription, earned him the title.

q: Which Indian city is popularly called the 'Pink City'?
exp: Jaipur's old city was painted pink in 1876 to welcome the Prince of Wales.

q: What is the state bird of Bihar?
exp: The house sparrow was declared the state bird of Bihar.

q: Who administers the oath of office to the President of India?
exp: Under Article 60, the oath is administered by the Chief Justice of India or the senior-most judge available.

q: Mining, fishing and agriculture belong to which sector of the economy?
exp: The primary sector extracts natural resources directly from nature.

q:
Match the battle with its year.
P. First Battle of Panipat   Q. Battle of Haldighati   R. Battle of Buxar
1. 1764   2. 1526   3. 1576
exp: Panipat I was fought in 1526, Haldighati in 1576 and Buxar in 1764.

q: The book 'Wings of Fire' is the autobiography of
exp: 'Wings of Fire' (1999) was written by A. P. J. Abdul Kalam with Arun Tiwari.

q: Who was the first Indian woman to win an individual Olympic medal?
exp: Karnam Malleswari won weightlifting bronze at Sydney 2000.

q: National Youth Day in India is celebrated on the birth anniversary of
exp: National Youth Day is observed on 12 January, Swami Vivekananda's birthday.

q: The national song of India, 'Vande Mataram', was composed by
exp: Vande Mataram appeared in Bankim Chandra's novel Anandamath (1882); Tagore wrote the national anthem.

q: Indian Standard Time is calculated on the basis of which longitude?
exp: The standard meridian 82°30′ E passes near Mirzapur; IST is UTC+5:30.

q: Dr. Rajendra Prasad, the first President of India, was born at Ziradei in which present-day Bihar district?
exp: Ziradei is a village in Siwan district.

q: Under which Article can the President proclaim a National Emergency?
exp: Article 352 deals with emergency due to war, external aggression or armed rebellion; 356 is State Emergency, 360 Financial Emergency.

q: Who is regarded as the Father of the Indian space programme?
exp: Vikram Sarabhai founded ISRO's precursor INCOSPAR; Bhabha is father of the nuclear programme.

q: Which of the following is a Kharif crop?
exp: Kharif crops are sown with the monsoon (June-July), e.g. paddy, maize; wheat, gram and mustard are Rabi crops.
